items.name: Raw Ironstone ore
items.reason: Abundant mixed iron-bearing cargo in an iron-rich world; transport, sorting and refining dominate its modest value.

items.name: Magnetite-rich stone
items.reason: Useful iron feed and magnetic research material has routine industrial demand, but abundant iron prevents a scarcity premium.

items.name: Silica-rich grit
items.reason: Ordinary grit is abundant bulk abrasive and silicate feed; no clean crystal or optical grade is specified.

items.name: Alumina-rich rock
items.reason: Candidate hard ceramic and electrical-insulation feed serves specialist heat and isolation needs; value comes from intended industrial use, pending composition qualification.

items.name: Carbonate stone
items.reason: Carbonate feed supports widely needed lime, binders and settlement construction; broad demand raises it above undifferentiated rubble without making it scarce.

items.name: Dry mineral salts
items.reason: Useful selected mineral feed has routine processing demand; culture compatibility remains unresolved and no nutrition or survival performance is certified.

items.name: Graphite-bearing stone
items.reason: The roster specifies sparse seams and candidate dry lubrication/conductive composites, giving specialist utility beyond ordinary rock; no ready conductor grade is implied.

items.name: Unprocessed copper-rich stone
items.reason: Better-conductor sources are strategically limited in this iron-rich world; unsorted copper-bearing rock has specialist prospecting value despite gangue and uncertain recovery.

items.name: Sorted copper-bearing ore
items.reason: Sorting concentrates a scarce better-conductor source for coils, contacts and control equipment, reducing useless cargo and making this high-value industrial feed.

items.name: Native copper lump
items.reason: Unworked copper metal addresses the conductor bottleneck more directly than mineral feed; its useful metal fraction supports valuable specialist electrical stock, pending qualification.

items.name: Tungsten-bearing ore
items.reason: Candidate wear-resistant material feed fills a specialist fabrication need; the lore does not establish a uniquely scarce tungsten deposit or a ready high-performance alloy.

items.name: Magnesium-bearing rock
items.reason: Identified magnesium-compound feed has ordinary refining potential, while uncertain grade and difficult recovery prevent a specialist-metal premium.

items.name: Unworked magnesium metal
items.reason: Manufactured unworked metal embodies specialist refining effort beyond raw compounds; intended fabrication value remains conditional on handling and material suitability.

items.name: Raw hematite
items.reason: An identified iron mineral still competes with abundant iron-bearing material; a species name alone gives no premium purity, yield or alloy performance.

items.name: Raw sulfur
items.reason: A broadly useful and relatively available industrial chemistry source supports separation, treatment and processing; utility is high but scarcity is modest.

items.name: Raw gypsum
items.reason: Accessible evaporite feed supports molds and mineral products with ordinary workshop demand; no rare formation or premium grade is specified.

items.name: Raw talc
items.reason: Candidate powders and ceramic feed have practical routine workshop uses, without evidence of exceptional scarcity or a finished-material premium.

items.name: Lead-bearing ore
items.reason: Identified heavy-metal feed has industrial utility but remains unrefined bulk cargo; no particular strategic application or rich grade is established.

items.name: Zinc-bearing ore
items.reason: Candidate alloying and protective-coating feed supports specialist material durability work; the rank reflects that use rather than an invented local deposit rarity.

items.name: Silver-bearing ore
items.reason: The roster targets a high-grade seam for specialist contacts; scarce better-conductor supply gives it high industrial value beyond its ornamental or trade appeal.

items.name: Gold-bearing rock
items.reason: The roster explicitly proposes scarce feed for specialist components and trade; limited precision/contact material and desirability support high value without assigning an Earth-market price.

items.name: Raw fluorite
items.reason: Specialist ceramic and metallurgical processing feed can enable controlled material work; exact mineral chemistry and recipes remain proposals.

items.name: Antimony-bearing ore
items.reason: Candidate specialist alloy feed has more focused industrial value than common iron cargo; neither deposit scarcity nor a finished alloy is certified.

items.name: Clear quartz
items.reason: Clear crystal offers selected ornamental and premium clear-stone potential beyond bulk silicate; it is not assumed large, flawless or qualified for precision optics.

items.name: Smoky quartz
items.reason: The current use is dark ornament and contrasting inlay; color alone does not establish scarcity, optical performance or high-value gem grade.

items.name: Garnet
items.reason: Distinctive selected gem material supports detailed settings and inlay; specialist ornamental value is provisional, with local abundance and cutting yield still open.

items.name: Spinel
items.reason: Selected hard-looking ornamental material is intended for polished accents and settings; provisional value follows that craft demand, not an assumed terrestrial rarity or special power.

items.name: Peridot
items.reason: Distinctive green ornamental material offers specialist decorative demand; deposit abundance and actual gem grade remain unapproved.

items.name: Tourmaline
items.reason: Candidate multicolor material serves distinctive regional ornament and settings; no additional electrical property or uniquely rare deposit is inferred.

items.name: Zircon
items.reason: Candidate brilliant accents and fine settings justify a selected ornamental-material band, while local abundance, clarity and cutting yield remain open.

items.name: Oxygen-releasing stone
items.reason: The author-established oxygen-releasing family has potentially high survival utility in the low-oxygen setting; this is a provisional value rank while output, depletion, activation and actual scarcity remain undefined.

items.name: Glowing stone
items.reason: The author-established light-emitting family has specialist portable-lighting utility; output, duration and abundance are unresolved, and light does not establish heat or fuel.

items.name: Flint stone
items.reason: Candidate sparking and worked-edge uses make this a useful everyday resource; appropriate fuel and atmospheric conditions are still required.

items.name: Feldspar fragments
items.reason: Useful glass and ceramic batch feed has routine kiln demand; no exceptional purity or deep-crystal grade is specified.

items.name: Obsidian chunks
items.reason: Potential cutting and scraping blanks offer immediate shaping utility above rubble; brittleness, selection and mounting limit their value.

items.name: Emery-bearing lumps
items.reason: Candidate abrasive grains support specialist finishing and repair; grade, hardness and contamination must still be checked before use.

items.name: Dense barite lumps
items.reason: A dense fabrication feed is useful cargo, but weight alone and an unresolved application do not justify a strategic-material premium.

items.name: Young surface Iron Growth fragments
items.reason: Young surface Growth is plentiful and easy to recover, with porous low-density material suited to analysis or processing rather than structural stock.

items.name: Mature formation Iron Growth pieces
items.reason: Mature Growth is the standard commercial industrial source, with real infrastructure demand and extraction effort but widespread bulk supply.

items.name: Dense old-growth mineral cores
items.reason: Centuries-old dense cores require costly depth access and offer premium composition-sensitive feed and research value; no particular core is certified as a master seal alloy or ancient synthetic.

items.name: Alkaline mineral crust
items.reason: Alkaline deposits are less abundant than sulfur and constrain useful cleaning, chitin processing and glaze chemistry; raw crust still requires assay and controlled preparation.

items.name: Nickel-bearing nodules
items.reason: The roster explicitly proposes scarce specialty-steel and electrical-contact feed; focused industrial utility justifies a specialist band without claiming a qualified alloy.

items.name: Tin-bearing gravel
items.reason: Candidate bronze alloying feed enables a specialist material route distinct from abundant iron; yield and deposit frequency remain proposals.

items.name: Chromite-rich stone
items.reason: Candidate alloying and refractory uses support specialist heat and wear applications; the raw stone is not already a performance alloy or certified refractory.

items.name: Ilmenite-rich sand
items.reason: The stated purpose is pigment and unspecified specialist mineral feed; no titanium-metal recovery process or exceptional deposit grade is established to justify a higher band.

items.name: Dolomite fragments
items.reason: Candidate lime and kiln-flux feed has broad practical demand but belongs to routine industrial mineral supply.

items.name: Halite chunks
items.reason: Salt is abundant bulk evaporite cargo with useful industrial chemistry demand; it has no rare-crystal premium and is distinct from culinary-qualified salt.

items.name: Agate nodule
items.reason: Candidate beads and small inlays provide ordinary ornamental value; a banded appearance alone does not prove rarity or exceptional gem quality.

items.name: Chalcedony seam stone
items.reason: Candidate carving and inlay material offers everyday decorative utility; translucency alone does not establish rare optical grade.

items.name: Culinary-candidate salt crystals
items.reason: Selection for a dietary candidate creates practical food-preparation interest beyond industrial salt, while composition and food suitability remain unverified.
